---
title: Configuration
description: >
  Configure formatting, linting, file selection, and external tools for a
  Panache project.
---

Put a `panache.toml` at the root of your project to share settings between the
CLI and language server. Every key is optional. This guide covers common setup
tasks; the [configuration reference](../reference/configuration.qmd) describes
the full configuration format, defaults, and discovery rules.

## Create a Project Config

Start with the settings your project needs:

```toml
extend-exclude = ["vendor/**", "_site/**"]

[format]
line-width = 88
wrap = "sentence"
```

Commit `panache.toml` so contributors use the same settings. Unknown keys are
errors. Add `#:schema https://panache.bz/panache.schema.json` at the top for
completion and validation in editors that support TOML schema directives. See
[editor support](../reference/configuration.qmd#editor-support) for other ways
to associate the schema.

For a project of plain Markdown files, set the flavor at the top level. For
example, a repository using GitHub-Flavored Markdown can use:

```toml
flavor = "gfm"
```

See [flavors](../reference/configuration.qmd#flavor) for Quarto, R Markdown,
MyST, and other formats, including filename-based selection.

## Choose the Configuration Source

Panache looks for the nearest project config while walking from the input file's
directory up to the repository root. It accepts `panache.toml`, `.panache.toml`,
and `.config/panache.toml`. If it finds none, it uses `PANACHE_CONFIG` when set,
then the platform's user config.

To select a file explicitly or try the built-in defaults:

```sh
panache --config path/to/panache.toml format document.qmd
panache --isolated lint document.qmd
```

For one formatting run, override a setting with
`panache format -o line-width=100 document.qmd`. Put persistent choices in the
project config. The [configuration reference](../reference/configuration.qmd)
describes precedence, global config locations, and how the language server
reloads them.

## Inspect a Document's Settings {#inspect-settings}

Use `panache inspect` to see the resolved flavor, configuration file and any
inherited files, and all extension states for a document:

```sh
panache inspect document.qmd
```

The `Effective` column includes configuration overrides; `Default` shows the
built-in value for the resolved flavor. This makes it easy to see whether an
extension override changes a default. Names use the same kebab-case spelling as
`[extensions]` in `panache.toml`.

To list a flavor's built-in defaults or inspect a one-off extension override:

```sh
panache inspect --isolated --flavor pandoc
panache inspect document.qmd -o extensions.east-asian-line-breaks=false
```

The command resolves settings from the path without reading the document or
stdin, so the file does not need to exist. With no file, it uses the current
directory's configuration; `--stdin-filename` supplies a document path when
needed.

For scripts, use `panache inspect document.qmd --json`. The JSON object contains
`flavor`, `configuration`, and `extensions`. Each extension has Boolean
`effective` and `default` values. The configuration records its `source`
(`explicit`, `discovered`, `env`, `global`, or `none`), `path`, and `chain` of
canonical paths, starting with the selected config and followed by its inherited
files. With no config file, `path` is `null`, and `chain` is empty.

## Share Settings Between Projects

Discovery selects a single config. Use `extend` to inherit another file:

```toml
extend = "../shared/panache.toml"

[format]
line-width = 100
```

The path is relative to the file declaring it. The project's values override
inherited values, and tables merge by key. See
[inheritance](../reference/configuration.qmd#extend) for how lists and flavor
overrides merge.

## Choose Files to Process

Use `extend-exclude` to skip additional paths during directory walks while
retaining the built-in exclusions:

```toml
extend-exclude = ["vendor/**", "generated/**"]
```

These patterns apply to formatting and linting. An explicitly named file is
processed unless you also pass `--force-exclude`:

```sh
panache format --force-exclude generated/example.md
```

See [file
selection](../reference/configuration.qmd#file-selection-directory-traversal)
for include patterns, `.gitignore`, and the directory that anchors each pattern.

## Configure Linting and Embedded Code

Use the [linting guide](linting.qmd#configuration) to enable or disable document
rules. Formatting and linting of embedded code are opt-in. For example, with the
Arity CLI installed on `PATH`:

```toml
[formatters]
r = "arity"

[linters]
r = "arity"
```

`panache format` now formats R code blocks, and `panache lint` checks them.
External linters use built-in presets with command and argument overrides.
External formatters also accept custom commands. See the [formatter
presets](../reference/formatter-presets.qmd), [linter
presets](../reference/linter-presets.qmd), and their configuration details in
the reference.

The [dprint plugin](integrations.qmd#dprint) uses `dprint.json` and does not
load `panache.toml` or launch external tools.
